instrument: Ordinance imposing a moratorium on development applications for data centers (first reading June 22, 2026; third reading Sept 21, 2026)
summary: Twelve-month moratorium on accepting, processing or approving development applications for data centers, defined as facilities of one megawatt or more of combined connected electrical load. Applications received after first reading are held in abeyance; projects with prior conditional plan approval or a development permit issued in the prior twelve months are exempt; extendable by council resolution. Floor amendments at third reading are recorded separately.
text: Data Centers are defined as a facility comprised of one or more buildings that houses computer systems and associated components, including telecommunications and data storages systems, that has a combined connected electrical load of one megawatt or more, and whose primary function is the storage, management and processing of data.

source.citation: Spartanburg County Council, Main Agenda - Final with backup, Sept 21, 2026, item XVII.A (ordinance as presented for third reading)

notes: CORRECTION: previous entry described the moratorium as applying only to facilities over 65 MW. The ordinance defines data centers at 1 MW; 65 MW is the ceiling of an exception added by floor amendment (see sc-spartanburg-county-moratorium-amendments). Pending Ordinance Doctrine invoked, so applications were held from first reading. The packet text is unamended (signature block still 'June 2026'). Same day, executive session item II.F: legal advice regarding litigation related to data centers (parties not named).
